title: College football quarterback tiers 2026: Ranking every projected starter from 1 to 138
content:
Projecting how a college quarterback will pan out often proves a fool’s errand, despite how many people have dedicated their livelihoods to trying.

But that doesn’t mean they’ll stop trying, because sometimes, you end up with a Fernando Mendoza, the one-time two-star recruit and Cal transfer who vaulted Indiana to a national championship and became the No. 1 pick in the NFL Draft.

So as the 2026 season approaches, we’re back to rank every projected starting quarterback in major college football in the second annual edition of The Athletic’s College QB Tiers.

For those unfamiliar, the inspiration for this comes from Mike Sando’s NFL QB Tiers. Our goal is to rank all 138 FBS starting quarterbacks to identify who experts believe are the best. This is not an NFL Draft ranking; we’re ranking them as college quarterbacks.

Our expert panel consisted of roughly three dozen coaches, general managers, personnel directors, scouts and front office staffers across the country, representing every conference. These people, who were granted anonymity so they could offer their honest opinions, gave us their thoughts on how quarterbacks in their league compared, what they think of players they’ve competed against and who the very best in the country are, regardless of conference. We relied heavily on this feedback to form the list. There was no formal point system or vote tally. We simply leaned on these experts for their insight.

Just like last year, we categorized the 138 quarterbacks into tiers. There is no fixed number for each tier; they are divided where separations felt natural based on feedback.

Although this isn’t a draft projection, we included draft analysis for some 2027-eligible prospects, courtesy of Dane Brugler and Nick Baumgardner.

Let the debate begin.

Notes: Snap counts, dropbacks, off-target percentages and pressure rates are from Pro Football Focus. Explosive play rates are from TruMedia. Because of the changing nature of NCAA eligibility rules, quarterbacks are listed by what year they’re in (first, second, third, fourth, etc.) rather than classification (freshman, sophomore, junior, senior).

Quarterbacks are sortable by conference and by their status: returning starter, transfer or new starter. Returning starters are those who generally started at least half of their current team’s 2025 games, with exceptions for QBs who were opening-day starters but lost extended time to injury. Transfers include only those who transferred to their current team in the 2026 offseason. New starters are mostly first-time starters and generally include QBs who haven’t started at least half a season before, but could also be former transfers who have been in their programs for multiple seasons and are now getting the chance to start.

For teams that haven’t officially named a starter because they’re still engaged in a quarterback battle, we ranked who we project to start based on information gathered to this point. For quarterbacks making their second appearance on this list, we included their 2025 College QB Tiers ranking.
